Threat.value: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place

Memory.value: When I try to deliberately remember what happened I find it difficult to access the memory
The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

vignette: Amir had spent most of his life working as a roofer, exposed to all sorts of elements and hazards. But it was one particular incident 10 years ago that changed everything for him. He was working on a project when he accidentally inhaled a toxic chemical while applying a new type of sealant. The fumes overwhelmed him, causing him to lose consciousness and fall off the roof. When he came to, his coworkers were frantically calling for an ambulance. As Amir recounts this event, it's clear that the sensory details are still vividly etched in his mind - the smell of the chemicals, the feeling of disorientation, the sound of his colleagues' panicked voices. But what frightens him most is not the memory itself, but how it has become intertwined with his daily life. He can't be around children without being suddenly transported back to that moment, worrying about their safety and his own vulnerability. Even seeing kids playing in a park or watching family movies with his grandkids becomes an ordeal. The media hasn't helped either. Any news report about industrial accidents or chemical spills sends Amir into a tailspin of anxiety. He'll watch the footage, mesmerized by the images of destruction and chaos, unable to shake off the feeling that it could happen again - this time to someone he loves. His wife, Fatima, has noticed how withdrawn Amir becomes after these episodes, how he'll pace around the house, his mind racing with worst-case scenarios. People who know about the accident also trigger a reaction in Amir. Coworkers from that fateful day will occasionally reach out, asking how he's doing or reminiscing about old times. But for Amir, their inquiries are like reopening an old wound. He'll become guarded and evasive, unsure of how to respond without unraveling. The physical consequences of the accident have also taken a toll on Amir's life. His startle response has become so pronounced that even a gentle touch from Fatima can send him into a panic. "I'm just resting my hand on your shoulder," she'll say, confused by his reaction. He knows it's irrational, but he can't shake off the feeling of vulnerability. As a result, Amir struggles to relax, even in safe spaces like his own home. His mind is always on high alert, anticipating potential dangers and threats. Sleep has become a luxury he can no longer afford; the memories of that day will creep into his dreams, forcing him awake with a jolt. When he tries to recall what happened deliberately, he finds himself hitting a mental block - as if his brain is trying to protect him from the trauma. But at other times, the memories come flooding back unbidden, like a nightmare he can't wake up from. The most disorienting part for Amir is when emotions overwhelm him without any clear memory or image attached. He'll feel an intense sense of dread or anxiety and won't know why. It's as if his body remembers what happened even when his mind doesn't. This has left him feeling disconnected from himself, unsure of how to navigate these unpredictable mood swings. Lately, Fatima has been urging Amir to seek help. She's noticed how his moods have become increasingly erratic and isolated. The incident 10 years ago was just the beginning; what followed was a decade-long struggle with anxiety, fear, and hypervigilance. As Amir finally begins to confront this reality, he's most afraid of losing himself completely - of becoming so consumed by these memories that he can no longer connect with his loved ones or find peace in his own home. He's hoping that therapy will help him reclaim some semblance of normalcy and learn to live alongside the shadows of that fateful day.
